posts.heading: September 20, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 233 feeder visits and 18 species, slightly busier than the 217 average for the past week. All eleven species recorded on each of the last seven days, including Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees, and Northern Cardinals, were present again.

Tufted Titmice led the count with 113 visits, while Northern Cardinals and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds each accounted for 14. A Tufted Titmouse visited the tube seed feeder, and a female Northern Cardinal perched on the station's metal bar.

Audio detections totaled 334, slightly above the weekly average, driven largely by Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals. Northern Mockingbirds, present every day until now, were absent today.

posts.heading: September 19, 2026
posts.text: The station recorded 213 visits from 18 species, slightly above the weekly average for species and visits, though detections dropped significantly to 224 compared to the previous week's average. This shift aligns with the audio source change to the pi-mic on September 13 and the installation of a new seed feeder the same day. Regulars like the Carolina Wren and Tufted Titmouse remained consistent, with the Wren leading in detections and the Titmouse in confident visual visits.

posts.heading: September 18, 2026
posts.text:
September 18 added up to a quiet day at the station, with 99 feeder visits significantly below the previous seven-day average of 199.7. The count of 17 species matched the weekly average, but the drop in physical traffic stood out against the 302 visits recorded on Thursday.

The subdued visitation aligns with the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which replaced an old unit that was causing bird detection problems. No new species were introduced by the audio switch to the pi-mic on September 13, and the station’s roster remained consistent with the week’s standard residents.

Mourning Doves, a regular presence for the last seven days, were absent today, as were Gray Catbirds and Northern House Wrens. The day closed with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird visiting just six minutes after sunset, marking the final visual record.

posts.heading: September 17, 2026
posts.text: The station logged 302 feeder visits and 20 species, marking the busiest day of the past week. While the preceding week averaged 169 visits and 15 species, Tuesday’s activity was lower than the recent peak, yet it remained well above the early-week baseline. Regulars like the Carolina Wren, Tufted Titmouse, and Northern Cardinal held their positions, with the Wren alone accounting for 132 detections.

posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 244 feeder visits and 20 species, exceeding the previous week's average of 137.7 visits and 14.0 species. This was the busiest day of the last seven, surpassing the 278 visits recorded on Tuesday, though Tuesday also saw 20 species. Tufted Titmice, Blue Jays, and Carolina Chickadees maintained their consistent presence, with Tufted Titmice contributing the highest number of visual visits.

The audio log reflected the switch from the c120 to the pi-mic that occurred earlier in the week. This change coincides with the continued detection of the Northern House Wren and Eastern Kingbird on the new microphone. No new species were heard for the first time at the station during this period.

Visual activity remained high, with the Tufted Titmouse seen 104 times and the Ruby-throated Hummingbird 36 times. The last visual sighting of a Ruby-throated Hummingbird occurred 6 minutes after sunset. The station's recent installation of a new seed feeder and the peanut refill in the treat bowl supported this level of bird interaction.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 278 visits and 20 species, marking the busiest day in the last week and far exceeding the recent average of 98 visits. Regulars like the Carolina Wren, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal remained prominent, with the Wren accounting for 126 detections. The increase in activity aligns with the installation of a new seed feeder and treat bowls earlier in the week, which have supported the rising visitor counts since the seed source change.

Among the sightings, the Eastern Phoebe was recorded as the first confident visual at this station. The audio log also captured a Common Gallinule. Other new additions to this week's list include a Cedar Waxwing and a Northern House Wren, both heard at least once during the day.

These detections follow the switch from the c120 to the pi-mic audio source on September 13, meaning these species are first heard on the new microphone rather than being new arrivals. The day saw consistent activity from dawn, with the first visual of a Tufted Titmouse six minutes before sunrise, until the last visual of a Carolina Chickadee 158 minutes before sunset.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text: The station’s activity outpaced the previous week’s average significantly, with 241 feeder visits and 16 species recorded compared to the prior seven-day mean of 63.6 visits and 10.0 species. This surge follows the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which resolved previous detection issues, and the switch to a new audio source the same morning. While Tufted Titmice remained the most frequent visual visitors with 97 confident sightings, Carolina Chickadees and Mourning Doves also contributed heavily to the visual counts.
